findings.title: Crash between gateway charge and local complete can double-charge after restart
findings.evidence: The function documents that a retry after a crash between the external charge and local completion should be deduplicated by the provider, but the implementation never persists any provider response before returning to local memory only. After a process restart, the in-memory store is empty, so a retry will call the gateway again and correctness now depends entirely on the provider honoring the same key.

findings.recommendation: Do not claim exactly-once semantics with an in-memory store. Either persist completion state durably before acknowledging success, or narrow the contract and docs to at-most-once per process lifetime / best-effort deduplication. If provider-side deduplication is required for correctness, handle and store the provider's idempotent replay response explicitly and document that dependency.

findings.title: Catching BaseException swallows process-termination signals and mutates state during shutdown
findings.evidence: The error path catches every BaseException, which includes KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, and GeneratorExit. On supported POSIX/Python runtimes this is reachable during shutdown or interruption, and the handler will run 'store.abandon' before re-raising, altering idempotency state in situations that should usually terminate immediately.
findings.recommendation: Catch Exception instead of BaseException so normal application errors release the in-flight key, while process-termination exceptions are not intercepted. If you need special cleanup on cancellation, handle only the specific exception types you expect.
